widgets.name: deep_mlp
widgets.title: What makes a deep network deep: stacking layers vs. adding bends
widgets.hint: Compare 0 Hidden (Part-1 Perceptron), 1 Hidden, and 2 Hidden layers · switch Unit bend to Linear (no bend) to see stacked layers collapse into one straight line · press play to watch training from scratch
widgets.pitch: Stacking layers without bends inside the units collapses back to Part 1's single straight line. Adding bends lets one layer place flat creases, while a second layer folds an already-folded space to carve nested boundaries.

widgets.name: manifold_untangle
widgets.title: Deep learning as disentanglement: unknotting tangled curves layer by layer
widgets.hint: Press play or scrub Depth to travel from input layer L0 to L4 · increase Tangle turns to tighten the spiral
widgets.pitch: Two intertwined spiral strands cannot be separated by any single flat cut in input space. Stacked layers gently loosen one loop at a time until a straight boundary separates them cleanly.

widgets.name: activation_splines
widgets.title: Bending the line: nonlinear hinges vs. linear collapse
widgets.hint: Switch activation between Linear, ReLU, GELU, and Tanh · press play to fit hidden hinges · drag knot handles along the axis
widgets.pitch: Combining straight-line units always produces another straight line. Giving each hidden unit a hinge or smooth bend (ReLU, GELU, Tanh) lets their sum curve locally around real developmental trajectories.
widgets.data_doc: {x: number[], y: number[], xlabel?: string, ylabel?: string}

widgets.name: xor_fold
widgets.title: The XOR problem: folding space so one straight line suffices
widgets.hint: Compare 0 hidden layers (linear) vs. 1 hidden layer · press play to train · scrub Fold morph to watch space crease
widgets.pitch: When category identity depends on an interaction (XOR or concentric rings), one hidden layer of hinges creases and folds the input plane so opposite corners land on the same side of a final straight cut.

widgets.name: mlp_backprop
widgets.title: Inside a tabular neural network: forward pass & error backpropagation
widgets.hint: Press play or step to run forward + backward updates · modulate playback speed · adjust predictor sliders to test live inputs
widgets.pitch: Spreadsheet predictors flow forward through weighted connections and hinges to form a prediction, then send the prediction miss backward so each connection updates according to its share of responsibility.

widgets.name: transfer_hierarchy
widgets.title: Transfer learning: reusing a visual hierarchy instead of starting from noise
widgets.hint: Switch regime between Frozen head, Full finetune, and Train from scratch · vary Labeled sample size N
widgets.pitch: Pretrained backbones arrive with edge, texture, and 3D part detectors intact. Locking the backbone and fitting a fresh final readout generalizes from small samples where training from scratch overfits.

widgets.name: llm_explainer
widgets.title: (GPT-Style) LLMs: from subword tokens to next-token trajectories
widgets.hint: Press play to trace tokens through attention layers · slide Attention head across all 12 heads · drag the 3D sphere or adjust Temperature
widgets.pitch: Words split into subword pieces and lookup IDs, map to number lists, gather context from earlier words through attention heads, and trace a path on the unit sphere toward the next word.
widgets.data_doc: {cases: {prompt, tokens, ids, candidates, logits, cand_xyz, traj_xyz, attentions}[]}

widgets.name: lora_adapter
widgets.title: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA): steering a frozen model through a narrow bottleneck
widgets.hint: Press play or scrub training from zeroed start to adapted model · slide Bottleneck rank to widen or pinch the side-channel · switch Headline or drag the 3D sphere
widgets.pitch: Locking the large pretrained weights in place and training a narrow hourglass side-channel steers the model's vector on the unit sphere using roughly 2% as many adjustable weights.

widgets.name: sae_superposition
widgets.title: Polysemantic neurons vs. monosemantic Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) latents
widgets.hint: Press play to sweep across topics and watch dense neurons mix vs. SAE latents isolate each theme · click any concept spoke or toggle 2 co-active concepts
widgets.pitch: Networks pack many themes into fewer units, making single units fire for unrelated topics. A Sparse Autoencoder expands dense hidden states into a wider checklist where only a few clear themes light up per input.

widgets.name: clip_alignment
widgets.title: Multimodal alignment: matching images & text on a shared unit sphere
widgets.hint: Press play or scrub training from random start to aligned CLIP space · click any row in the 5×5 similarity table to highlight its image–caption pair on the 3D sphere · drag the sphere to rotate
widgets.pitch: Contrastive training (CLIP / SigLIP) pulls paired pictures and captions together along the diagonal of the similarity table while pushing mismatched pairs apart around the unit sphere.

widgets.name: relative_reps
widgets.title: Relative representations: linear classification over natural-language anchor queries
widgets.hint: Toggle anchor queries to grow or shrink the spanned region on the sphere · watch the great-circle decision boundary & accuracy update · drag the 3D sphere
widgets.pitch: Scoring each image by its similarity to plain-English anchor phrases turns hundreds of unnamed coordinates into a small table where every classifier weight attaches directly to a readable phrase.
widgets.data_doc: {queries: string[], query_xyz: number[][], img_xyz: number[][], sim: number[][], y: int[], class_names: string[]}

widgets.name: layerwise_readout
widgets.title: Encoding & decoding across network depth: probing a Vision Transformer
widgets.hint: Press play or scrub Layer to move from the patch stem to the final norm · toggle right view between Beauty scatter and Layer RDM
widgets.pitch: Cross-validated linear regressions on OASIS aesthetic ratings and linear classifiers on SimpleShapes across Vision Transformer layers, paired with held-out scatters and pairwise distance matrices.
widgets.data_doc: {layers: string[], oasis_curves: {beauty, valence, arousal}, shapes_curve: number[], beauty_scatter: object, rdms: object}

widgets.name: trifecta_explorer
widgets.title: Types of deep learning models: sensory diet ⇒ architecture ⇒ objective
widgets.hint: Choose which Trifecta factor to vary · click any opportunistic experiment card beneath the sphere or use the toggles · press play or drag the 3D hypersphere
widgets.pitch: Single-panel left-to-right pipeline from Sensory Diet to Computational Architecture to the Latent Hypersphere, paired with opportunistic model-zoo controls below.
